summary: Health-probe drain abort prevents model-pin commit and causes silent fallback to legacy variant
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary promote for BeaconPay's dedicated pool, the health-probe drain sequence aborted the model-pin commit on control-plane leading to silent routing of a portion of sessions to the legacy variant. Impact: ~3% of requests from BeaconPay's production tenant received responses from the older model (quality regression) for ~18 minutes. No 5xxs were reported but customer observed inconsistent outputs. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in prod/us-west-2; canary weight 10%; model promote in progress; tenant pinned to new model expected after commit.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a staged canary promote with weight 10% and pin-commit mode enabled. 2) Trigger a rolling drain of one edge instance (simulate prewarm/eviction). 3) Observe canary commit logs and control-plane commit ACK sequence. 4) Repeat with probe timeout set to 2s on the edge health check. Expected: pin commit either succeeds or explicit rollback. Observed: commit aborted on probe-drain sequence without rollback signal and routing silently reverted for some sessions.
logs:
Selected log excerpts:
- control-plane: pin_commit: id=promote-2026-03-12-09:14 status=initiated
- orchestrator: commit_ack: id=promote-2026-03-12-09:14 ack=partial missing_coordinator=egress-42
- edge-proxy: probe: instance=egress-42 drain=started timeout=2s probe_abort=true
- routing: route_decision: tenant=beaconpay cohort=canary -> fallback=legacy-variant (no explicit unpin event)
- serving-runtime: request-log: tenant=beaconpay model=legacy-variant request_id=...
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge health probe abort during drain closed the pin commit window on the coordinator before the control-plane persisted the pin. The orchestrator treated the partial ack as failure and silently retried routing decisions, but some session-affinity tokens had already been stamped with new pin metadata by the edge before rollback path executed. We saw missing 'rollback' signals in the commit trace. Correlated with a recent edge change that introduced a fast probe-abort path when drain + probe timeout occurred. Verified through matching timestamps between probe_abort and missing commit ack. Related PR that altered probe behavior: control-plane PR #2145.
root_cause: Race between edge probe drain abort and control-plane pin commit persistence. The edge abort prevents the final coordinator ACK from reaching the control-plane within the commit window, leaving a partial commit state that the routing layer interprets inconsistently across replicas. No explicit rollback or reconciliation ran within the pin grace period, so some sessions continued with legacy routing while others used the partially-applied pin metadata.
workaround: 1) For affected tenant (BeaconPay) temporarily increase canary commit grace window by 30s and pause automated edge drains for their dedicated pool. 2) Apply manual reconciliation: force-persist pin state from control-plane for pending promote id, then restart affected edge instances to clear partial stamps. Implemented for BeaconPay at 2026-03-12 09:40 UTC — customer reports quality normalization.
resolution_notes: Short-term fix: rolled back the fast-probe-abort change on edge-proxy in prod us-west-2 and increased default pin commit window from 5s to 20s for dedicated pools. Long-term: orchestration change to require explicit commit/rollback broadcast and idempotent reconciliation of partial states (tracked in GH PR). Plan created for automated verification: post-commit reconciliation job that verifies cohort routing coherence. Follow-up task INT-... created to implement audit metric for 'partial_commit_events'.
